seal.statement: The push gate cannot report success, or be run, without having proven what it claims. (G1, R23) gateExactSha (scripts/checks/push-gate-corpus-worktree.js) and the publisher's gateExactHead (scripts/publish-head.js) run the gate in a checkout inside the enclosing repository's test-output/; a gate command that removed or replaced the checkout's .git link made the post-run status read discover the ENCLOSING repository, which ignores test-output/, and pass (exit 0, stray files and all). Now one identity owner in publish-head.js (checkoutIdentity / exactCheckoutStatus) records the checkout's .git link, the gitdir it resolves to and HEAD = the gated sha before the run and compares them after; every read stops discovery at the checkout (gitProcessEnvironment(base, checkout) sets GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES, also exported to the whole gate run) and the status is read through the recorded gitdir; identity lost is the typed refusal checkout-identity-lost, diagnostics are kept and nothing is stranded (removeWorktree prunes after the directory is gone). (G2) A stop request is honoured: the gate installs no signal handler (one only replaced the default action while spawnSync blocked, swallowing a SIGTERM sent to the gate alone), so the gate ends by the signal; its command runs under a supervisor (the gate script, --supervise) in its own process group, which forwards signals and, when the gate process is gone, stops the group, keeps the diagnostics and removes the checkout; a checkout stranded outside that window records its owner and is released by the next gate. (G3) Every gate, publisher, solver and lab entry point with side effects refuses an argument it does not know, with a usage line and a non-zero exit, before any work (push-gate-change-proof.js --help ran the whole placed corpus). (G4) retainGateDiagnostics never prunes the run it just wrote, prunes only sha-named entries, and orders by mtime then name. (G5) The runner echoes a failing test's stdout and stderr indented and line-terminated, so no echoed line can be read as a runner verdict, summary, plan, retried-once or relayed line by any reader (TEST_FILE_LINE's owner).

G2 design. Evaluated: (a) keep handlers - impossible to act while spawnSync blocks, the signal is swallowed (status quo); (b) default action + cleanup-on-next-run only - the gate ends at once but its command runs on orphaned in the checkout for up to the whole corpus; (c) chosen: no signal handler in the gate (default action ends it, by the signal: the parent sees SIGTERM) + its command runs under a supervisor = this script again (--supervise <checkout> --gate <sha> --run ...), which spawns the command detached (own process group), forwards SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP to the group, polls process.ppid every 100 ms and, when the gate is gone, stops the group (TERM, KILL after 5 s), keeps the diagnostics and removes the checkout; and (b)'s sweep for the two short synchronous windows outside the command (making / releasing the checkout): every gate checkout's mkdtemp parent holds 'gate-owner' (pid sha), and each gate start releases (retain + remove) any checkout whose owner pid is dead; the supervisor re-claims the record before its own release so a concurrent sweep skips it. gateExactSha stays synchronous; the command's group no longer gets the terminal's Ctrl-C directly - the supervisor forwards it.
